On 1/17/77, a check was made with several laundries
that specialize in martinizing in the Seattle area, and it
was learned that laundry tickets are customarily stapled to
trousers and other items as they are received from the customer
for cleaning. The number and letters on these tickets correspond
with a code which is a sequential numbering system. 'The first
character in the code is an alphabetic letter and the second
character in the code.is a number, ranging from 1 to 10,000.

When a customer brings in an item for cleaning,
such as a pair of trousers, he fills out a cleaning form
requesting cleaning and putting his name on the form. The
date of pickup and the cross reference. number also appears
on this form. The number on the form could be A-1 through
10,000 and a corresponding tag would then be stapled to
the trousers with that number A~l through 10,000, so that
the trousers could be located in the event the customer
does not show up to claim his cleaning items.

Most laundries vary the first letter from A-1 through
10,1000 to B-1 through 10,000, etc., until the end of the year,
at which time they normally start over again-with A-1 through
10,000; however, this is not a hard and fast rule and with
just a number such as found on the trousers in this case,
. A-317, it would be impossible to determine who the customer
was who had the trousers cleaned. It might be possible in
some cleaning establishments to determine the customer if
the trousers were recently cleaned by checking past ticket
